items.title: Tesla deploys record 13.5 GWh of storage in Q2
items.summary: Tesla reported deploying 13.5 GWh of energy storage globally in the second quarter of 2026, a sharp jump from the prior quarter and from Q2 2025, making it the company's second-largest quarterly total ever. The results come ahead of Tesla's July 22 earnings call, where investors will focus on the recently announced VPP partnership with Sunrun and Renew Home offering flexible power to hyperscalers and grid operators.

items.title: Eos lands Pentagon deal, posts record quarterly revenue
items.summary: Zinc-battery maker Eos Energy Enterprises announced a strategic partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense aimed at bolstering national defense infrastructure resilience, alongside preliminary Q2 results showing its highest quarterly revenue ever despite continued losses per unit sold. Separately, developer Frontier Power USA said it will deploy Eos's Z3 technology at the 100MW/400MWh Wildfire BESS project in Texas as part of a roughly 1.8GWh capacity build-out.

items.title: Giga Storage financially closes 2.8 GWh Belgian project
items.summary: Belgian developer Giga Storage secured financing for its Green Turtle battery energy storage project, with construction now scheduled to begin in September following financial close on July 9. The 2.8 GWh facility ranks among the largest battery storage projects announced in Belgium to date.

items.title: BYD, Envision advance gigawatt-scale European BESS projects
items.summary: BYD Energy Storage and Greenvolt Power announced plans to jointly develop a 600 MW/2.4 GWh storage facility in Siedlce, Poland, with construction slated to start in the third quarter of 2026 and operation targeted for late 2027. In Germany, Envision Energy and Elements Green will deploy a 400 MW/1,600 MWh four-hour system using Envision's Gen 8 platform to support grid flexibility.

items.title: Moment Energy opens world's largest EV battery reuse plant
items.summary: Moment Energy opened Megafactory 1 in Vancouver, described as the world's largest facility dedicated to repurposing retired EV batteries into modular energy storage systems for critical infrastructure. The launch reflects growing industry momentum around battery circularity as manufacturers seek to extend the useful life of second-life cells.

items.title: Unigrid launches 25-year sodium-ion home battery in Europe
items.summary: Battery maker Unigrid unveiled its NaCasa sodium-ion home battery system in Europe, rated for a 25-year lifespan and pitched as a safer, mineral-independent alternative to lithium-ion for residential solar and backup power. The company plans a U.S. rollout pending regulatory approval, joining Peak Energy and ESS Inc among American firms racing to commercialize sodium-ion for stationary storage.

items.title: Peak Energy to build first US grid-scale sodium-ion factory
items.summary: Sodium-ion startup Peak Energy said its $71 million California factory will be the first U.S. facility dedicated to grid-scale sodium-ion energy storage systems, with shipments expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. The move reflects accelerating domestic interest in sodium chemistry as a hedge against lithium price volatility and import dependence.

items.title: Scientists crack solid-state battery's core failure mechanism
items.summary:
Researchers published in Nature identified how soft lithium dendrites fracture the hard ceramic electrolyte inside solid-state batteries, a mechanism that has long triggered short circuits and hampered commercialization. 
Researchers solved the mystery of how soft lithium dendrites crack the hard ceramic inside solid-state batteries, triggering short circuits, and the breakthrough could help engineers build safer, longer-lasting batteries for smartphones, electric vehicles, and other electronics.

items.title: China's solid-state battery sector hits tonne-level scale-up
items.summary:
During the week of July 10-16, China's solid-state battery industry crossed a key threshold as sulfide material producers prepared 100-tonne-class production lines for Q3 commissioning, moving the sector from lab-scale to industrial trading volumes. 
The inaugural year of all-solid-state battery industrialisation verification begins, and 2027 demonstration vehicle installations have already become an industry consensus,
 with new cells from Zhongke Yuanben (342 Wh/kg) and Farasis Energy (500 Wh/kg) launched in the same week alongside major R&D investments from Chery and FAW.

items.title: Chinese sodium-ion cell matches Tesla-grade battery quality
items.summary: A peer-reviewed teardown study found that a commercial sodium-ion battery from Chinese manufacturer Hina achieved production quality and design features comparable to Tesla's lithium-ion cells. Researchers say further gains in cold-weather charging and energy density could position sodium-ion as a cheaper, more abundant alternative for both EVs and large-scale grid storage.

items.title: FERC orders new reliability rules for data center loads
items.summary: At its July 16 open meeting, FERC directed the North American Electric Reliability Corporation to develop new reliability standards addressing risks from integrating large computational loads such as AI data centers into the bulk power system, with compliance filings due by December 31, 2026. The commission also acted on multiple transmission tariff and rate matters affecting utilities including Southern California Edison, PG&E, and Southwest Power Pool.

items.title: Grid operators face July deadline on large-load integration
items.summary: Following FERC's show-cause orders issued in June to all six regional grid operators under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act, RTOs and ISOs must submit detailed reports by the end of July on how they will ensure adequate generation for growing data center and large industrial loads. Analysts say the orders effectively favor storage and other flexible, deflationary technologies over slower-to-build generation.
